metadata.hardware_requirements: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a com-puting server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores).

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.

nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Mentioned as used for calibration, but no specific source or access path is provided.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are extracted as (x, y) points from raw traffic video frames within a defined control area.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, no tools named, parameters not stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Form position matrices from vehicle locations
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m₁ ∈ RXxY; m₁ (x, y) = Uv, i∈ Iť, where Uy is a constant and I refers to the set of vehicles in the control area at time step t.
nodes_process.description: A position matrix m_t is created for each time step t. Cells corresponding to vehicle locations are set to a constant Uv, and other cells are zero. Signal state information is also included.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, parameters not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s₁: S₁ = {m₁-(N-1),..., m₁}. For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive position matrices are stacked to form the traffic state s_t. Down-sampling is applied to reduce input dimensions for computational efficiency.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, N_time_steps_to_stack stated, down_sampling_factor not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: A deep Q-network is defined, consisting of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers followed by two fully connected (FC) layers. One FC layer calculates the Q-value, and the other predicts speed and queue length for multitask learning.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r₁ after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, μ > 0, ω < 0, where v and q represent the average speed in the merging area and the average queue length at the on-ramp during time step t and t + 1, respectively.
nodes_process.description: The reward function r_t is defined as a linear combination of the average speed in the merging area (v_t) and the average queue length at the on-ramp (q_t), with weights mu and omega.

nodes_process.source_quote: The total loss function is as follows: L (w₁) = L₁ (w₁) + λL2 (w₁). L₁ (w₁) = Esa((rt+1 + ymax, Qº (st+1, a', w¯ ) – Qº (s, a, w;))²), L2 (W₁) = Es,a((Q¹ (s, a, w₁) – v)² + (Q² (s, a, w₁) – u)²)
nodes_process.description: The total loss function is a weighted sum of two components: L1 for Q-value estimation and L2 for prediction accuracy of speed and queue length (multitask learning).

nodes_process.node_name: Train deep Q-network for ramp metering
nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update w; to minimize the loss function. The experience replay [30] stores the data prepared for training into the replay buffer and samples these data uniformly for training the agent. The target network [29] is introduced for a stable estimation of target value Q* (s, a). Algorithm 1: Deep Q-learning for ramp metering.
nodes_process.description: The deep Q-network is trained using the Adam optimizer to minimize the defined loss function. Experience replay and a target network are employed to stabilize training. A multitask learning strategy is used to simultaneously predict Q-values, speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, most parameters stated (number_of_training_episodes, number_of_decision_time_steps_in_episode not stated).

nodes_process.node_name: Set up microscopic traffic simulation environment
nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, as shown in Figure 5. The speed limits in the mainline and at the on-ramp are 80 and 40 km/h, respectively. The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO, modeling a freeway section in Qingdao, China, including a one-lane on-ramp and a three-lane mainline. Speed limits are defined, and driving behavior parameters are calibrated using empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/1 tool named, 2/3 parameters stated (driving_behavior_parameters not specified).

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate DRL method performance in simulation
nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: The trained DRL model is evaluated within the SUMO simulation environment over 20 experiments, each initialized with different random seeds. Performance metrics such as travel times, queue lengths, and traffic flows are collected.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, 1/2 parameters stated (random_seeds not specified).

nodes_process.source_quote: For comparative purposes, two scenarios are also considered in the evaluation. The first scenario does not apply ramp metering...
nodes_process.description: A baseline scenario where no ramp metering is applied is evaluated in the SUMO simulation environment. Performance metrics are collected for comparison.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, 1/2 parameters stated (random_seeds not specified).

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles. The ramp metering rate rk for k-th cycle is given by the following: rk = rk-1 + KR[ok − ô] – Kp[0k-1 − 0k], (13)
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA ramp metering method is evaluated as a baseline in the SUMO simulation environment. The method calculates the ramp metering rate based on downstream occupancies and previous cycle's red phase length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/2 tools named, most parameters stated (random_seeds not specified).

nodes_process.node_name: Perturbation analysis of video data information
nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas. The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea. Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is performed by dividing the control area into eight subareas. Information from each subarea is systematically removed from the original video data to generate perturbed data. The DRL model is then evaluated with this perturbed data to assess the impact of information from different subareas on performance.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, no tools named, 2/3 parameters stated (random_seeds not specified, method of removal not detailed).
